the deep water of the South Pacific Ocean is flowing northward at a mean rate of 0.5 to 1.0 centimeters per second.

(1) the deep flow is northward in the eastern Pacific and southward in the western Pacific, (2) it is strongest at the equator, (3) its velocity decreases rapidly as the distance from the equator increases, (4) its velocity is greater at the equator in the western Pacific than in the eastern Pacific, and (5) it is strongest in the upper 1,500 m.
